title: doctor and --version write the index they only read: plain git status in git_head_identity, fullcycle and release_dirt takes the optional lock
body:
## Finding

A devbin read path writes into the repository it reads. The defect class is one: a git call that compares the work tree to the index, made without `--no-optional-locks`, takes git's optional index lock and rewrites a stale index. That can fail a peer's concurrent commit with `index.lock exists`, and every estate runs devbin beside live nodes that commit.

**Where the fleet saw it: each estate's own `project.referent`, not devbin's code.** dc's read-only doctor sweep of the 14 swept estates on 2026-09-21 (hold 16, vc decision 25, hv's go) found `find -newer` a marker listing `.git` after doctor in Gtools and Intent. A no-op control over the same window listed nothing, and a second doctor run reproduced it in both. An xtrace of Gtools's doctor puts both of its git calls at `bin/devbin`'s referent eval: Gtools and Lamplight declare `project.referent` as a pipeline running plain `git rev-parse --short HEAD` and `git status --porcelain`, and Intent declares `bin/.devbin/cmd/measured --value`, its own handler, which runs `git status`. The dispatcher evals the referent on EVERY devbin invocation, so every command in those three estates can take the lock, not only doctor. **doctor itself is green on today's code** in a stale fixture with no referent. dc first attributed the sweep's write to `git_head_identity`, which was wrong, and corrected it the same morning. Sweep outputs are under `tmp/dc/doctor-sweep/` (not committed).

**devbin's own read paths have the same defect,** found by the tests written for the fix: `--version` (through `git_head_identity`), `fullcycle`'s header and `release_dirt` (read by the read-only `release check`) each rewrite a stale index. vc reproduced the mechanism independently in a scratch repo: with stale stat info, plain `git status --porcelain` rewrites `.git/index`, and `--no-optional-locks` or `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` writes nothing. A fresh index has nothing to refresh, which is why the effect comes and goes.

## Population and predicate

Predicate: a git call that compares the work tree to the index (`status`, `diff` without `--cached`) on a read path, invoked without `--no-optional-locks`. Measured on a stale-stat fixture (commit a file, then `touch` it), with a no-op control that writes nothing:

| Command shape                                          | Writes `.git/index` |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- |
| `git status --porcelain`                               | yes                 |
| `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`   | yes                 |
| `git diff --name-only`                                 | yes                 |
| `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain`           | no                  |
| `git diff --cached --name-only`                        | no                  |
| `git rev-parse --short HEAD`                           | no                  |
| `git ls-files`                                         | no                  |

Sites in `lib/` that match the predicate (3):

1. `lib/helpers` `git_head_identity`: `git -C "$root" status --porcelain`. It is reached from `version_identity` (`--version`), from `cmd/devbin`, and from `cmd/fullcycle`'s HEAD line. doctor does not reach it.
2. `lib/cmd/fullcycle`: the `dirty:` count, `git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" status --porcelain`.
3. `lib/release.steps` `release_dirt`: `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`. It is reached from `release check`, which is read-only, and from the cut and `release status`.

Sites excluded, with the reason for each:

- `lib/cmd/check`'s `git diff --cached --name-only` compares the index to HEAD and was measured to write nothing.
- `lib/release.steps`'s `git read-tree` runs under a private `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, so it writes only its own temporary index.
- `rev-parse`, `ls-files`, `cat-file`, `for-each-ref`, `merge-base`, `symbolic-ref`, `config --get` and `check-ignore` do not refresh the index (`rev-parse` and `ls-files` were measured).
- `git add`, `git commit`, `git tag` and `git checkout` in `cmd/release` are the cut's deliberate writes.
- The existing `git_readonly` callers are already guarded.

## Fix

1. Move `git_readonly`, `git_readonly_prime` and `_DEVBIN_GIT_LOCAL_VARS` from `lib/install` to `lib/helpers`, as their ONE home. `bin/devbin`, `cmd/release` and `cmd/fullcycle` source `lib/helpers` but not `lib/install`, and every file that sources `lib/install` sources `lib/helpers` first. No second copy.
2. Route `git_head_identity` and fullcycle's dirt read through `git_readonly`. `release_dirt` takes the LOCK property only, `git --no-optional-locks status`, and leaves git's environment alone (vc's review): release's writes (`git add`, the commit, the tag) honour an inherited `GIT_DIR`, so a dirt read that cleared it would check one repository and commit into another. Whether release should refuse an inherited `GIT_DIR` outright is a separate question, and not this issue's.
3. `git_head_sha` also goes through `git_readonly`. Locks do NOT justify this, because `rev-parse` takes none. The property it buys is that **one identity line reads one repository**. `git_head_identity` reads the sha through `git_head_sha` and the dirt through `status`. If only the status moved, an inherited `GIT_DIR` (or any of git's local env vars; the list is `git rev-parse --local-env-vars`, as `git_readonly` already reads it) would point the sha at one repository while the dirt read the one at `root`. The line would then pair a sha with a `+dirty` from a different tree. Clearing the env also makes `-C root` mean what the caller passed: the repository at `root`, never one an inherited variable names. `git_head_sha` is issue 0014's shared git axis, used for build stamping, so this changes its behaviour only under inherited git env vars. It is named here so a reviewer can refuse it separately from items 1 and 2.
4. The referent eval in `bin/devbin` exports `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, git's environment form of `--no-optional-locks`, inside its own `$(...)`, so it reaches the referent alone and never a gate. A referent is a value composer by contract, so a read-only default fits it. The override is the referent's own: one that sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1` itself gets the lock back. No change is needed in any estate. The core sites keep their own fixes (items 2 and 3), so each concern has one home and there is no env blanket over the dispatcher.

## Test

Red first. The fixture has to be a stale-stat repository, because a fresh index cannot go red. A control proves that the fixture does make plain `git status` write. Then `--version`, `doctor` and a referent running plain `git status` leave `.git` untouched: `find -newer` over the whole of `.git`, the index included, lists nothing. The same referent setting `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1` itself does write, which is the control and the override in one. The same holds for `git_head_identity`, fullcycle's dirt read and `release_dirt` at the function level. A case with an inherited `GIT_DIR` pointing elsewhere shows `git_head_identity`'s sha and dirt reading the repository at `root`. A second one shows `release_dirt` reading the repository release writes to.

Lands in 0.1.3. Reviewed by vc before it lands.

## Resolution

Fixed at `faf5be7` as the Fix section above describes, items 1 to 4, reviewed by vc. `tests/unit/readonlygit.bats` carries 11 arms; each fixed site is killed by its own arm under mutation. Targeted run over 20 files: 903 ok, 0 not ok (not the full suite, which runs at the 0.1.3 cut's gates). Ships in 0.1.3; the Gtools, Lamplight and Intent referents stop taking the lock with no change on their side.
